rule: For each metric M in {CER, WER} and each pair (LIF vs BiGRU seeds, LIF vs MLP seeds, MLP vs BiGRU seeds): the per-seed value is the mean over the four evaluation seeds; the difference D = mean(baseline seeds) - mean(candidate seeds) in percentage points, positive = candidate better; the 95% interval is Welch's t on the two seed samples. A win on M is claimed only if the interval excludes zero. Reported alongside, never as the claim: wins-of-N (candidate seeds whose eval-mean beats the baseline's seed mean), training-seed spread (max - min of the per-seed means), eval-seed spread. The deployed 5-seed BiGRU ensemble and the committed snn_fetu.pkl / ff_fetu.pkl are separate rows, not sample members. Pre-registered 2026-09-16 before any Exp 206 model was trained. Exp 207 amendment (pre-registered 2026-09-17 before any temperature was fitted): every row carries its own temperature T, chosen from CALIB['grid'] as the value minimising decoded CER on the calibration corpus (seed 4242, per_fist 250; ties to the smaller T); WER at that T is reported, not optimised. T is applied to the Q16.16 log-posteriors as ((T_q*lp)+32768)>>16 on the host exactly as a device would. The language-model insertion bonus beta stays 2.5. The oracle uses confidence ORACLE_CONF. The claims rule above is then applied at each row's calibrated T; the same rows at T = 1 are re-reported so the effect of calibration is visible.
